claimed_value: RAG over an adversarial scenario corpus (Sentence-BERT, FAISS) with few-shot, chain-of-thought prompting makes an LLM write a DSL; a middleware converts it to Python for highway-env; PPO agents then train ego and adversary behaviour.
DeepSeek-V3 DSL score 80.17 on 6 held-out scenes (R1 73.83, Qwen2.5-Plus 63.33); collision rate about 8% above baseline; trained ego avoidance lowers collision rate by roughly 30% on average.
Learned score network ranks 32 candidate adversary paths; best path gives goals for a reactive hierarchical policy that picks skills from an adversarial prior in a VAE skill space.
Not a controllability test. SEAL-trained ego policies average a 21.5% increase in Success rate over the top baseline in each setting; ablations show learned objective and skill policy both needed.

Each prompt is encoded and pooled per agent, then added to that agent's policy query. Text goes through a LoRA-finetuned LLaMA3-8B producing language-conditioned queries, summed into the policy token.
Goal Point prompt gives ADE 0.3882 m, 59.12% gain over no prompt; Text prompt 26.96% gain; all prompt types together 0.2877 m ADE, 69.71% gain.

VLM directly edits a rule-based baseline trajectory (CTRV model fused with map waypoints), followed by B-spline smoothing, sigmoid fusion with the baseline, and an LQR controller for kinematic feasibility.

Edited trajectories have smaller minimum distance to ego and more extreme acceleration and steering than directly generated ones. Ego policy gains 13.3% and 25.3% route completion and 28.5% and 39.4% lower crash rate versus VLM-RL and CAT.
Decoupled two stages: optimisation finds the adversarial goal, then a goal-conditioned motion prediction model fills in realistic intermediate trajectory toward that goal, with dynamic replanning.

Ablation on nuScenes: without intention transfer collision is 1.4; with optimised transfer 40.6 at 10.4 global off-road; random-interpolation goal gives 75.9 collision but 24.1 global off-road. Waymo RL planner: 45.3 vs CAT 36.7.

Hierarchical policy: goal generator proposes a fixed route goal fed to a goal-conditional policy and discriminator; parallel beam search prunes the least realistic half of branches by discriminator score, and results are distilled back.
No controllability experiment; evidence is realism and diversity. On proprietary data BC collision rate drops from 16.65% to 1.84% with tree search, and hierarchy restores diversity.

Courtesy coefficient is an input to the trajectory generator; training uses auto-labeled courtesy values, data augmentation with predicted trajectories, and a differentiable courtesy loss. A range predictor normalizes values per scenario.

Full model reaches CourtesyMSE 0.120 with range-predicted values; generated courtesy correlates with input quantile at 0.60 on the full interactive validation subset and 0.79 on the high-courtesy subset.
Not a control mechanism: unconditional DDPM generates a rasterized BEV initial scene (map plus agent states), vectorized by a graph method; a trajectory prediction model then rolls out futures.

No controllability experiment. Closest evidence is distribution matching: map plus agent initial states at 80m give FID 46.81 and diversity discrepancy 1.25%; same initial scene yields distinct futures qualitatively.

Pipeline: map and traffic retrieval, behaviour models plus adversity orchestrator and NADE for agent trajectories, rendered HDMap videos feed ControlNet branches of Cosmos-Drive with VLM text prompts for multi-view video.

Qualitative only: case studies (Ann Arbor roundabout, Mcity cases, five worldwide examples) show video motions following simulated trajectories and weather or roadwork variations; no quantitative number.

Risk embedded by an MLP into a 128-dimensional latent, concatenated with the diffusion step embedding at every layer; trained with condition dropout and sampled with classifier-free guidance scale omega.
Mean crash rate rises from 20.6% to 50.6% as desired risk increases; PET below 0.4 s density rises 113%, from 0.030 to 0.064, from low to high risk.

Pretrained world model is fine-tuned with constrained closed-loop multi-agent RL to a coarse correlated equilibrium; constraints enforced through a Lagrange multiplier, risk via CVaR, with a regularizer toward observed behavior.

Lower alpha gives faster, more aggressive, shorter-headway driving; higher alpha gives lower speed and larger spacing. Tighter distance constraints raise the Lagrangian penalty. Average diversity 2.0 versus 0.58 for second best.

Gradients of a spatial, temporal and jerk guidance loss during diffusion denoising modify only the adversarial agent's trajectory; the world model, with a causal interaction graph, handles other agents' responses.
At 8-10 s horizon, CR is 22.7% versus 12.3% for CCDiff, with lower ADE (1.877 vs 2.092). Minimal ablation variant drops to CR 6.5%.
